waypoints.name: Cascade Pass Road (near trailhead)
waypoints.directions: Follow Cascade River Road to its end at the Cascade Pass Trailhead, about 3,600 ft. In a heavy snow year the road can be gated well below the trailhead — one party found it gated at mile 18 with the road snow-free above to the last hairpin, and biked that section — so budget for the possibility rather than assuming you can drive to the end. Before you leave the car, look up: the couloir is the obvious deep gash between Cascade Peak on the left and Johannesburg on the right, in full view from the parking lot and the last road switchbacks. Judge whether the snow is continuous from here, in daylight, and be willing to turn around at the car.

waypoints.name: Base of CJ Couloir
waypoints.directions: Walk back down the road from the trailhead, anywhere from a quarter mile to just under a mile, then drop down a dirt and brush embankment into the valley and cross the Cascade River, often still snow-covered in spring. Cross the terminal moraine and a snowfield to the continuous snow apron at the foot of the couloir, about twenty minutes from the road.

waypoints.name: East ridge gain
waypoints.directions: Climb about 3,000 ft of snow up the couloir, moving early and never stopping in the choke, where a bulge of water ice may need a belay or can sometimes be passed on a narrower line to the right. Above the choke go up and left, then straight up the final couloir to the Cascade-Johannesburg col; a cornice there has been passed against the rock of Cascade Peak on the left.

waypoints.name: Johannesburg summit
waypoints.directions: From the col climb the steep east side on heather, talus and broken rock bands, mostly Class 3-4, past rock horns to a red dike, then up a steep gray gully of about 500 ft to the false summit. Drop about 30 ft and traverse loose south-side ledges roughly 75 ft below the crest, in and out of ribs and gullies, to a deep slot-gully that gives a final Class 3-4 pitch to the true summit.
